headline: Ruffa Gutierrez on Herbert Bautista, ex-husband Yilmaz Bektas, and finding love again
snippet: Is Ruffa Gutierrez ready to fall in love again? The actress, TV host, former beauty queen, and model is happy being single for now, but she is not closing her doors to romance. Ruffa was previously in a relationship with actor-politician Herbert Bautista. Although they have since gone their separate ways, they remain friends and still keep in touch. “We still talk though not as regularly as we used to, but yeah, we call each other sometimes,” she said. Ruffa also maintains a good relationship with her former husband, Turkish businessman Yilmaz Bektas, with whom she shares two daughters, Lorin and Venice. The former couple have worked on building a better co-parenting arrangement over the years. “We are much okay now, friendlier. But nothing more. I don't fantasize about rekindling anything,” she said. But what if either Herbert or Yilmaz wanted to win her back? “I think if ever, they have to woo me. And hard. They have to make me fall for them all over again before I even consider the matter,” Ruffa said. For now, she is enjoying being single and having the freedom to make her own plans. She is open to meeting someone new, but she is not in a hurry to date. “You know what, I'm really happy being single. I don't have to think of anything or anyone before I do things. Hindi ko kailangan magpaalam for whatever. I'm happier, tsaka more structured ang schedule ko to what suits me,” she said. Ruffa is leaving the possibility of another relationship to God. She may be ready to date again next year, but she has other plans in the meantime. “I'm ready for whomever God brings into my life. I'd probably open up to dating again next year. Not now, I'm still having fun. I'm even planning pa a trip to Europe with my friends,” she shared. At 52, Ruffa is also embracing another stage of life. More than three decades after representing the Philippines at Miss World 1993, where she finished as second runner-up, she remains a familiar face in Philippine entertainment. She has built a career as an actress and TV host while raising her daughters. When it comes to growing older, Ruffa said she does not see it as something to fear. “It's inevitable. It happens to everyone. You shouldn't be afraid of it. You embrace it. Acceptance is key,” she said. Ruffa also shared her thoughts on what makes a woman beautiful. “For me, being beautiful radiates from within, so you have to feel beautiful to be beautiful. One thing I could say is, do away with stress, detox from negativity, focus on self-love. These are the things you should be mindful of,” she said. Motherhood remains one of the most fulfilling parts of her life. Ruffa is grateful for the women her daughters, Lorin and Venice, are becoming. “I'm really happy and fulfilled being a single mom. I am so grateful that my daughters have grown into such wonderful people. Of course, as their mom, I will always be there whenever they need me, but at the same time, I allow them space for growth,” she said. She also hopes people will give her daughters the chance to make their own names instead of constantly comparing them to her. “It's hard for them sometimes to read people comparing them to me, to what I have achieved at a young age, and it's really unfair. They're their own people, and you know, I'm glad that they aren't affected as much na. They're confident and beautiful in their own way,” Ruffa said. And while she believes beauty starts from within, Ruffa also sees the value of caring for one's skin, especially as women get older. She said she personally uses Biostile products, which she now endorses. “I tried them, of course. I don't endorse anything I haven't personally tried. Siyempre, we have to try din naman to put an effort in nourishing our skin, something that these products do, and amazingly so,” she said.

headline: How to Write Release Notes People Actually Read
snippet: People read release notes that tell them what got better for them. Group the notes by what people do in your app, lead every line with what they get, and leave out anything they never saw. Your AI can draft all of it from your pull requests. The free AI starter kit we build our own products with writes notes this way on every release. Group by what people do Follow the path a person takes through your product, in the order they take it. Write each heading as "When you ...": When you first open the app When you do the main task, with a heading for each main task When you organize or find your work When you change what the app uses, like sources, plans or connections Settings The look everywhere, for changes that touch every screen Skip any heading with nothing new under it. Lead every line with what the user gets Under each heading, write one bold line with the outcome, then a few bullets with the specifics. Write "The model list opens straight away", never "Virtualized the remote model list". Use a real number only when it's true and checked, like "about half a second, down from nearly three". Leave out what nobody saw Cut bugs you made and fixed inside the same release, test data, developer tools and internal checks. If a user would never notice it, it doesn't belong in the notes. Keep it short One line under the title, then the headings. Speak to "you", in short sentences and everyday words. No component names, no code names, no closing summary. Before and after Before After Refactored the auth flow You stay signed in after an update Fixed race condition in sync Notes you write offline show up on your phone Updated dependencies Leave it out unless users notice a change Misc bug fixes List the fixes people would notice, or leave the line out Get the release notes tool we use The starter kit turns your review notes and pull requests into release notes grouped by what people do, in your product's voice, and puts them at the top of the release. Get the starter kit free on GitHub. Questions How should release notes be organized? By what people do in your app, in the order they do it, like when you first open the app, when you do the main task, and settings. Skip any heading with nothing new. What should each release note line say? What the user gets, in plain words. Write "The model list opens straight away", never the technical change behind it. Can AI write release notes from pull requests? Yes. Give it the pull request comments and commit messages, tell it to group changes by user task and lead with outcomes, and have it drop anything users never saw. Originally published at wednesday.is.

Rigid 90s hairstyles have collapsed completely: what replaced the frozen look of the past
snippet: The sleek, lacquered perfection of the modern minimalist braid is yielding to a different standard. The blowout is back, but it has shed the rigid, frozen structure that defined the 1990s iteration. The contemporary version prioritizes movement and an unforced texture, relying on structural architecture rather than heavy fixation to maintain its shape. This shift demands a precise understanding of where the hair begins and how specific technical interventions create the final form. The foundation of this volume is established before any heat is applied. The physical state of the hair shaft determines how it will react to styling. To achieve the desired lift, the weight of the product must be managed strictly. Cleansing is targeted at the scalp and roots, while hydrating treatments are confined to the lengths to prevent the root zone from becoming weighed down. This separation of functions ensures the base remains buoyant. Finishing the wash with cooler water serves a specific mechanical purpose: it helps settle the cuticle, reducing friction and allowing the strands to slide with less resistance, which is a prerequisite for a smooth, light finish. The transition from wet hair to a styled form is governed by thermodynamics. Heat does not hold the shape; it merely makes the hair plastic. The structure is only set when the strand cools. Releasing a strand from a round brush while it is still hot results in immediate collapse under its own gravity. The critical operational step is the application of cold air. By switching the dryer to a cold setting for several seconds while the hair is still on the brush, the internal bonds lock into the new position. This thermal setting is the difference between a temporary lift and a lasting structure.
